title: I released a Steam game in 2015. Eleven years later, AI helped me return to game development. My new demo is out.
author: WalkingDadPG
selftext:
In 2015, I released Super Snow Fight on Steam. I kept wanting to make another game, and this year I finally picked up that old hobby again.



Claude Code and Codex have been a big part of that return. I have a programming background, but being able to work through code and try ideas with these tools made taking on another game feel possible. I've also used AI for artwork and audio.



The result is Fallen Nights, a zombie survival game where you scavenge during the day, build defenses, and survive the night. Your defenses and your escape boat need the same scrap, so spending more to survive also means staying longer.



One thing I learned along the way: getting a feature working doesn't mean it belongs in the game. I tried free building placement, then replaced it with fixed building spots to keep the decisions simpler and the action easier to read. A lot of the work has been testing and reconsidering what I'd already built.



The free Steam demo is now live. The full game is still in development, but having something people can download on Steam again is a milestone I wanted to share. The trailer also shows other locations; the demo takes place in Riverside.



Play the demo on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5177150/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5177150/)



If you enjoy it, you can wishlist the full game there too. If you'd prefer to try it in your browser: [https://fallennights.com/](https://fallennights.com/)



For others building with AI: what have you ended up removing or simplifying after actually playing your game?
